headline: ASX surged 1.37% to close above 8,844 today while gold hit a new high near $4,187 USD — your portfolio got a boost from PLS, TTWO, and MSFT last night.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO climbed 1.87% last night, continuing its strong run on GTA 6 hype. Forbes published a piece calling it a 'rebel strategy' — the market is betting the GTA 6 launch will be one of the biggest entertainment events ever. Your position is now up over 11% overall.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS was today's standout, jumping 1.95% at the close. Sentiment in lithium is improving — competitor Mineral Resources reportedly restarting lithium mines signals the industry thinks prices may be bottoming. Still well underwater overall (down ~22%), but today was a step in the right direction.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 1.62% last night, outperforming the broader NASDAQ. Earnings are coming up and analysts are previewing what to expect — the market seems optimistic, possibly reflecting confidence in Microsoft's AI products like Copilot driving revenue growth.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.57% today, riding a strong ASX session. As a diversified fund holding Australian and global shares, it benefited from the broad market rally.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.17% today. Emerging markets were fairly quiet — a small positive move in line with a mild risk-on day globally.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI was essentially flat today, up just 0.06%. The AI ETF tracks global AI companies — with the NASDAQ soft last night, there wasn't much fuel for a bigger move. Still down about 11% overall, so worth keeping an eye on upcoming US tech earnings.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.42% today. This ETF mirrors the US total sharemarket, and last night's NASDAQ was soft (down 0.8%), which weighed on VTS's ASX price today. The AUD also ticked up slightly, which can mildly reduce the AUD value of US-focused holdings.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 0.48% last night. Nothing dramatic — the slight dip may reflect some rotation out of Google into Microsoft as the market anticipates both companies' earnings. Alphabet's earnings preview is circulating and investors seem cautiously positioned ahead of the result.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL didn't move today, closing flat. Oil prices were barely changed overnight (WTI crude around $68.78 USD), so global energy stocks had no real catalyst. The IEA has flagged that the Iran situation is reshaping the oil market outlook, but uncertainty is keeping prices in a holding pattern.

watch_today.title: GOOG & MSFT earnings coming — big moment for your US holdings
watch_today.detail: Both Alphabet (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT) have earnings previews circulating. These results are approaching and will be the biggest catalyst for both stocks in months. GOOG slipped slightly last night while MSFT rose 1.62% — the market is already positioning. Hold both and watch the earnings dates closely.

watch_today.title: TTWO riding GTA 6 momentum — still a hold
watch_today.detail: Take-Two rose 1.87% last night and Forbes is running big pieces on the 'GTA 6 strategy'. Your position is up over 11%. The GTA 6 launch remains the key catalyst — no reason to sell ahead of that, but it's priced for a lot of optimism so don't add at these levels.

watch_today.title: PLS bouncing — lithium sector showing signs of life
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 1.95% today, its best session in a while. Mineral Resources restarting lithium mines is a signal that the sector thinks prices are near a floor. PLS is still down 22% in your portfolio — hold and monitor whether this is the start of a real recovery or just a dead-cat bounce.

watch_today.title: Gold hit $4,187 USD — a new high, and it matters for your portfolio
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 1.81% last night to nearly $4,187 USD per ounce. This is a safe-haven signal — investors are nervous about something (likely geopolitical tension and US fiscal concerns). Worth noting your VDHG and VGE have some indirect exposure, and it reinforces holding diversified assets.

watch_today.title: GXAI still underwater — watch US tech earnings for a re-rate
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF is down ~11% overall and barely moved today. The big swing factor will be US tech earnings (Google, Microsoft, and others in the index report soon). If AI revenue numbers impress, GXAI could get a meaningful lift. Hold for now and reassess post-earnings.

watch_today.title: ASX had a cracking day — up 1.37%
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 closed at 8,844 today, up 119 points or 1.37%. That's a strong broad-market day that lifted most of your local holdings. The AUD also rose slightly to 69.4 US cents, which is a mild headwind for the AUD value of your US stocks.

markets.summary: The ASX had a strong session today, closing up 1.37% at 8,844 — a solid broad-market rally. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 was virtually flat but the NASDAQ dropped 0.8%, dragged by some softness in tech names. Gold was the big story last night, surging nearly 2% to around $4,187 USD — a new high, suggesting investors are seeking safety. Oil was barely changed. The Aussie dollar ticked up to about 69.4 US cents.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech sold off mildly last night

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surged to a new high last night

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Barely moved — market in a holding pattern

politics.summary: No Australian political stories were available in today's data feed. This may reflect a quiet news day locally given it's a Saturday.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by the global tug-of-war over regulation — with the US heading toward a hands-off approach while Europe, Kenya, and the Philippines all push for tighter rules. There's also a practical angle: multi-model AI access is getting cheaper for consumers.

stories.title: Trump will oppose heavy US AI regulation, says outgoing tech adviser
stories.why_it_matters: The outgoing White House tech adviser has confirmed that the Trump administration will actively resist heavy-handed AI regulation in the US. This means American AI companies like Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI will likely face far fewer restrictions than their European counterparts, potentially giving them a competitive edge. For your GOOG and MSFT holdings, a light-touch regulatory environment is a tailwind — less compliance cost, more freedom to deploy AI products at scale.

stories.title: AI outpaces regulation, Europe's top bankers and regulators warn
stories.why_it_matters: Europe's top banking and financial regulators are sounding the alarm that AI is being adopted in finance far faster than any rule-making can keep up. This creates a risk: AI-driven trading and lending decisions are happening without clear guardrails. For investors with global exposure (like your VDHG or VGE), this is worth monitoring — financial instability driven by unregulated AI in European banks could ripple through markets.

stories.title: Kenya Artificial Intelligence Bill proposes new regulator, risk-based rules
stories.why_it_matters: Kenya is drafting a dedicated AI law that would create a new government regulator and apply different rules depending on how risky an AI system is (think stricter oversight for AI used in healthcare or policing versus a chatbot). It's part of a broader global wave of countries trying to get ahead of AI risks. Interesting context for the emerging markets exposure in your VGE — African tech regulation is starting to mature.

stories.title: Ditch ChatGPT — get Claude, Gemini, and 17+ AI models for life for $55
stories.why_it_matters: A lifetime deal is circulating that gives you access to Claude, Gemini, GPT, and more than 17 other AI models all in one place for a one-time payment of around $55 AUD. For everyday users tired of juggling multiple AI subscriptions, this is worth knowing about. It signals the AI tools market is getting commoditised — which is good for consumers but could pressure the subscription revenue models of individual AI providers.

sport.summary: Panthers thumped the Rabbitohs last night in Round 18, GWS snapped Fremantle's AFL win streak in a big upset, and Melbourne demolished Hawthorn in Tasmania. Wimbledon is underway with Alex de Minaur looking well placed after an open draw.

stories.title: Panthers 36 def. Rabbitohs 14 — comfortable Round 18 win
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith put Souths to the sword last night at CommBank Stadium, winning 36–14 in what was a one-sided affair. The Panthers continue to look ominous in 2026. The Rabbitohs' top-8 hopes take a hit with this kind of scoreline.

stories.title: How rugby league became Australia's most valuable football code
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News has published a deep-dive on how the NRL has overtaken AFL, soccer, and rugby union to become Australia's most commercially valuable football code. The piece examines broadcast rights, crowd numbers, and sponsorship — timely reading as NRL Round 18 gets underway this weekend.

stories.title: Melbourne Demons destroy Hawthorn in Tasmania — AFL shock result
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne put on a stunning performance against Hawthorn in Tasmania, winning convincingly in what 7NEWS called a 'destruction'. The result is a shock given Hawthorn's strong season form. Melbourne fans finally have something to cheer about after a tough stretch.

stories.title: GWS break AFL's biggest win-streak — Fremantle star Docker injured
stories.why_it_matters: GWS Giants snapped Fremantle's impressive win-streak — reportedly the AFL's biggest active run — in a major upset. Making it worse for the Dockers, a star player was injured during the match. No confirmed name or injury timeline in the available data, but it's a significant blow to Fremantle's top-of-ladder ambitions.

stories.title: No excuses for De Minaur: Wimbledon draw opens up for Australia's star
stories.why_it_matters: Alex de Minaur has landed a favourable draw at Wimbledon 2026, with Sporting News saying there are 'no excuses' for the Aussie to go deep in the tournament. Several higher seeds have already exited, clearing a potential path for De Minaur. Meanwhile, Cruz Hewitt — Lleyton's son — is competing in the juniors draw, carrying the family name at the All England Club.
